reproduced.finding: Legacy receipt verifier accepts an attacker-constructed reviewer JSON containing task_id, source_sha256, verdict REVIEW_OK and reviewer name qwen3:4b without verifying an actual model invocation or an independent REVIEW-owner signature.
reproduced.scope: Mocked GitHub read-only responses satisfying the expected commit-path and branch ancestry; attacker would need control of the trusted published receipt, so not proof of unauthorized writes to real GitHub.

reproduced.finding: Duplicate JSON keys in reviewer receipt are parsed last-wins, allowing a REVIEW_BAD then REVIEW_OK override without duplicate-key rejection.
reproduced.scope: Mocked accepted evidence, not a verified real publisher or real branch exploit.

positive_controls: Historical writer source byte digest remains checked.
Tests use local mocked API and never access real GitHub publishing endpoints.
requirements_before_integration: Do not rely on reviewer-model string and REVIEW_OK receipt fields as independent approval.
Use exact immutable GitHub Actions run/job/artifact with original raw Qwen output and source-bound bytes; owner REVIEW must issue separate tracked approval.
Use strict duplicate-key rejecting JSON and fixed schema, validate source and provenance before giving CORE a trusted boolean.
Do not use any historic module or mixed draft PR #2 as a production publisher without refreshed independent tests and coordinator approval.
Separately verify exact once-only publication with one unique task id and readback after uncertain response; old tests do not prove this.

independent_review_support.github_api_lookup_mode: fixed https GitHub REST read only, owner approval never granted automatically
